label: Luke 4:1
text: Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan, and was led by the Spirit into the wilderness

label: Luke 4:2
text: for forty days, being tempted by the devil. He ate nothing in those days. Afterward, when they were completed, he was hungry.

label: Luke 4:3
text: The devil said to him, “If you are the Son of God, command this stone to become bread.”

label: Luke 4:4
text:
Jesus answered him, saying,
“It is written, ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.’”

label: Luke 4:5
text: The devil, leading him up on a high mountain, showed him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time.

label: Luke 4:8
text:
Jesus answered him,
“Get behind me Satan! For it is written, ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and you shall serve him only.’”

label: Luke 4:9
text: He led him to Jerusalem, and set him on the pinnacle of the temple, and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, cast yourself down from here,

label: Luke 4:10
text:
for it is written,
‘He will put his angels in charge of you, to guard you;’

label: Luke 4:11
text:
and,
‘On their hands they will bear you up,
lest perhaps you dash your foot against a stone.’”

label: Luke 4:12
text:
Jesus answering, said to him,
“It has been said, ‘You shall not tempt the Lord your God.’”

label: Luke 4:14
text: Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit into Galilee, and news about him spread through all the surrounding area.

label: Luke 4:15
text: He taught in their synagogues, being glorified by all.

label: Luke 4:16
text: He came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up. He entered, as was his custom, into the synagogue on the Sabbath day, and stood up to read.

label: Luke 4:17
text: The book of the prophet Isaiah was handed to him. He opened the book, and found the place where it was written,

variants.note: Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke (Luke 4:17): ἀναπτύξας ('unrolled') in א (Sinaiticus), D(c), K, Δ, Θ, Π, Ψ, f1, f13 and the Byzantine text, against ἀνοίξας ('opened') in B, A, L, W, Ξ, 33, 892 and others.

label: Luke 4:18
text:
“The Spirit of the Lord is on me,
because he has anointed me to preach good news to the poor.
He has sent me to heal the broken hearted,
to proclaim release to the captives,
recovering of sight to the blind,
to deliver those who are crushed,

label: Luke 4:19
text: and to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord.”

label: Luke 4:20
text: He closed the book, gave it back to the attendant, and sat down. The eyes of all in the synagogue were fastened on him.

label: Luke 4:21
text:
He began to tell them,
“Today, this Scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”

label: Luke 4:22
text: All testified about him, and wondered at the gracious words which proceeded out of his mouth, and they said, “Isn’t this Joseph’s son?”

label: Luke 4:24
text:
He said,
“Most certainly I tell you, no prophet is acceptable in his hometown.

label: Luke 4:25
text: But truly I tell you, there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the sky was shut up three years and six months, when a great famine came over all the land.

label: Luke 4:26
text: Elijah was sent to none of them, except to Zarephath, in the land of Sidon, to a woman who was a widow.

label: Luke 4:27
text: There were many lepers in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet, yet not one of them was cleansed, except Naaman, the Syrian.”

label: Luke 4:28
text: They were all filled with wrath in the synagogue, as they heard these things.

label: Luke 4:29
text: They rose up, threw him out of the city, and led him to the brow of the hill that their city was built on, that they might throw him off the cliff.

label: Luke 4:30
text: But he, passing through the middle of them, went his way.

label: Luke 4:31
text: He came down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee. He was teaching them on the Sabbath day,

label: Luke 4:32
text: and they were astonished at his teaching, for his word was with authority.

label: Luke 4:33
text: In the synagogue there was a man who had a spirit of an unclean demon, and he cried out with a loud voice,

label: Luke 4:34
text: saying, “Ah! what have we to do with you, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know you who you are: the Holy One of God!”

label: Luke 4:35
text:
Jesus rebuked him, saying,
“Be silent, and come out of him!”
 When the demon had thrown him down in the middle of them, he came out of him, having done him no harm.

label: Luke 4:36
text: Amazement came on all, and they spoke together, one with another, saying, “What is this word? For with authority and power he commands the unclean spirits, and they come out!”

label: Luke 4:38
text: He rose up from the synagogue, and entered into Simon’s house. Simon’s mother-in-law was afflicted with a great fever, and they begged him for her.

label: Luke 4:39
text: He stood over her, and rebuked the fever; and it left her. Immediately she rose up and served them.

label: Luke 4:40
text: When the sun was setting, all those who had any sick with various diseases brought them to him; and he laid his hands on every one of them, and healed them.

label: Luke 4:41
text: Demons also came out of many, crying out, and saying, “You are the Christ, the Son of God!” Rebuking them, he didn’t allow them to speak, because they knew that he was the Christ.

label: Luke 4:42
text: When it was day, he departed and went into an uninhabited place, and the multitudes looked for him, and came to him, and held on to him, so that he wouldn’t go away from them.

label: Luke 4:43
text:
But he said to them,
“I must preach the good news of God’s Kingdom to the other cities also. For this reason I have been sent.”

label: Luke 4:44
text: He was preaching in the synagogues of Galilee.

variants.note: Cambridge Bible for Schools and Colleges on Luke 4:44 (biblehub): 'Here א, B, C, L and other uncials have the important various reading "of Judaea."' The WEB follows the Alexandrian 'Galilee'.

label: The devil: 'command this stone to become bread'
statement: The devil challenged Jesus, 'If you are the Son of God, command this stone to become bread.'

label: Jesus quotes Deuteronomy 8:3 against the first temptation
statement: Jesus answered the first temptation by quoting Deuteronomy 8:3: 'Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.'

label: Jesus quotes Deuteronomy 6:13 against worshipping Satan
statement: Jesus answered the temptation to worship the devil by quoting Deuteronomy 6:13: 'You shall worship the Lord your God, and you shall serve him only.'

label: Jesus quotes Deuteronomy 6:16 at the temple pinnacle
statement: Jesus answered the temple-pinnacle challenge by quoting Deuteronomy 6:16: 'You shall not tempt the Lord your God.'

label: Jesus returned to Galilee in the power of the Spirit
statement: After the temptation Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit into Galilee, and news about him spread through the surrounding area.

label: Sabbath synagogue custom: standing up to read
statement: In Nazareth, where he had been brought up, Jesus entered the synagogue on the Sabbath 'as was his custom' and stood up to read.

label: A scroll of Isaiah was handed to Jesus and unrolled
statement: The book (scroll) of the prophet Isaiah was handed to Jesus in the Nazareth synagogue; he unrolled it and found the place he wanted.

label: Jesus reads Isaiah 61:1-2 in the Nazareth synagogue
statement: Luke records Jesus reading Isaiah 61:1-2, with 'recovering of sight to the blind' inserted and the reading stopping before 'the day of vengeance' (61:2b).

label: Rolling up the scroll, returning it to the attendant, sitting
statement: Jesus closed (rolled up) the scroll, gave it back to the attendant, and sat down, while the whole synagogue looked at him.

label: The Nazarenes ask 'Isn't this Joseph's son?'
statement: The Nazareth congregation testified about him and asked, 'Isn't this Joseph's son?'

label: Famine with the sky shut 'three years and six months'
statement: Jesus described a great famine over all the land in the days of Elijah, 'when the sky was shut up three years and six months'.

label: Elijah sent to the widow of Zarephath in the land of Sidon
statement: Jesus said Elijah was sent to none of the widows of Israel except to Zarephath, in the land of Sidon, to a woman who was a widow.

label: Of many lepers in Israel only Naaman the Syrian was cleansed
statement: Jesus said there were many lepers in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet, yet none was cleansed except Naaman the Syrian.

label: The Nazareth crowd led Jesus to the brow of the hill to throw him off
statement: The Nazareth synagogue crowd, filled with wrath, rose up, threw Jesus out of the city and led him to the brow of the hill on which their city was built, intending to throw him off the cliff.

label: Demons cry 'You are the Christ, the Son of God' at the evening healings
statement: At the sunset healings in Capernaum demons came out of many, crying 'You are the Christ, the Son of God', and Jesus rebuked them and did not allow them to speak.

label: Sent to preach the good news of God's Kingdom to other cities
statement: Jesus said, 'I must preach the good news of God's Kingdom to the other cities also, for this reason I have been sent.'
